title: Cycle Compression Protocol — mid-cycle triage heuristics and staffing swaps
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Purpose: Define a lightweight, deterministic protocol for compressing cycle scope and reallocating staffing when an unexpected staffing shock occurs mid-cycle. The goal is to enable predictable, low-friction decisions that preserve OKR-critical work while limiting churn for engineering teams.
Scope: Triage heuristics, role shadowing rules, micro-commit lanes, timebox rules for scope cuts, communication templates for stakeholders, and automation for tracking capacity budget. Out of scope: changes to hiring plan or long-term roadmap priorities.
Why now: Recent incident where two engineers left product and caused ripple scope-slides across three squads; teams spent >48 hours debating priorities instead of shipping urgent bugfixes.
Success metrics: (1) median decision time for mid-cycle scope cuts reduced from 24h to <4h, (2) % of OKR-critical tasks preserved in compression events >=90%, (3) fewer ad-hoc cross-team reassignments requiring >2 weeks ramp time.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc with step-by-step decision checklist published in Confluence
Two-week simulation run with at least three product teams producing a compression decision and annotated outcomes
Automation: a capacity dashboard card that shows remaining commit points and flags when thresholds hit
Communication templates (Slack + all-hands blurb + customer status) stored in Drive

Risks: Over-automation may freeze judgement; to mitigate, protocol includes a 'human override' step requiring sign-off from PM + EM.
